transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um... my mom made the appointment. Mostly because I just... I can't make myself do anything anymore. I just sit in my room all day in the same clothes. I used to do things—like knit, or write in my journal, or go for walks—but I just don't do any of that now. And when my mom asks me what's wrong, I just... I barely have the energy to even answer her. So she brought me here.
Have you ever felt this way before in the past, perhaps months or years ago, or is this the first time you have ever felt this low?
Um... no, I don't think so. I think this is the first time. I don't remember ever feeling this... empty before. I always used to do things, so... yeah, this is the first time it's been like this.
Have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people don't seem to notice?
Um... no. I haven't heard anything like that. Or seen anything either. It's really just... quiet. I haven't noticed any voices or anything weird.
Have you noticed any changes in your physical movements, like feeling as though you are moving in slow motion or, conversely, feeling so restless that you cannot sit still?

Um... no, not really. I don't think I'm moving slower or anything. And I'm definitely not restless. I just... I sit there. I don't really move much at all, but it doesn't feel like slow motion. It's just... I don't want to move.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight since you started feeling this way?

Um... no, not really. I think I'm eating about the same amount as usual. I haven't noticed any changes in my weight, either. I just... I eat whatever is there, I guess. Nothing has really changed with that.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns, such as having trouble falling asleep or waking up much earlier than you intended?

Um... no, my sleep has been pretty normal. I usually just go to bed and sleep through the night. I haven't really had any trouble falling asleep, and I wake up around the same time I always do. So... no changes there.
How much difficulty are you having with your daily responsibilities, such as schoolwork or taking care of your basic hygiene, compared to how you functioned before you started feeling this way?

Um... I'm having a lot of difficulty, actually. I had to stop moving forward in my certificate program. I just... I'm not able to handle the practicum right now. And I can't really plan for the clinic office job I was working toward, either. Everything just kind of stopped. I just can't do it right now.
Do you find yourself feeling worthless, or do you often blame yourself for things that have gone wrong in your life lately?

Um... no, not really. I don't think I feel worthless, and I don't really blame myself for things. It's just... things are just happening. I don't feel like it's my fault or anything like that. I just... I don't feel that way.
About how long has it been since you started feeling this way and stopped doing your usual activities?
Well, I guess... this whole decline, all of this happening... it's been going on since I started the community-college program. So that's been about two years and two months ago.
During these past two years, would you say you have felt down or sad most of the time, for most days?
Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think I've felt sad or down most of the time. It's not like that. It's more just... everything else that's going on, but not really feeling sad.

When you think about the activities you used to enjoy, like knitting or writing, does it feel like you aren't interested in doing them anymore, or does it feel like you just don't have the physical energy to start them?

I think... mostly I just can't make myself do anything anymore. It's like I just don't have the energy to start. I just sit in my room with the same clothes on. I don't knit or write in my journal or go walking like I used to. Even when my mom asks what's wrong, I... I barely have the energy to answer her.
Do you find that you have any desire or interest in spending time with other people, or do you find yourself preferring to be completely alone?

I prefer to be completely alone. Like I was just saying, I really just sit in my room all the time. I don't have the energy to be around people or try to do anything with them. Even with my mom... like I mentioned, I can barely even talk to her when she comes in to check on me. So, no, I don't have any interest in seeing anyone else.
When you are sitting in your room alone, do you find that your thoughts tend to get jumbled or disorganized, making it difficult to follow a train of thought?

Um... no, I don't think so. My thoughts don't really get jumbled up like that. I mean, when I'm just sitting there, I'm not really... I don't have a lot going on in my head to get disorganized, I guess. It's mostly just kind of quiet. So, no, I haven't noticed having a hard time following a train of thought.
When you are around other people, do you feel uncomfortable or anxious, or do you just feel indifferent toward them?

I guess I just feel... indifferent. I don't really feel anxious or scared or anything like that. It's more like I just don't care. I don't feel any connection or reason to be around them, so I just... don't want to be. It's just easier to be by myself.
Do you find that you have any unusual beliefs or experiences, such as feeling like you have a special connection to certain events or that you can sense things others cannot?

Well, I do have this one thing. Since I was taking those college classes, I've just known that the school portal and the people running the clinic practicum were sending me messages. Like, they were using these little wording changes in emails and assignment comments to mark me as someone they don't want in healthcare. My mom says they're just regular messages, but I know what they're actually saying.
Do you feel that these messages you are receiving are part of a larger, organized plan or conspiracy that is specifically targeting you?

Yeah, I mean... like I was just saying, it's definitely a plan to target me. The people running the clinic practicum and whoever runs the school portal, they're doing it together. They're purposely using those little wording changes in my emails and the assignment comments to mark me, so I can't be in healthcare. My mom keeps telling me there's no plan and that they're just normal messages, but... I know they're organized and working together to keep me out.
During these past two years, have there been any periods where you felt unusually high, irritable, or had so much energy that you didn't need to sleep?

No, I haven't had anything like that happen. I don't really get those high feelings, and I definitely don't have so much energy that I stop sleeping. I just... my energy is pretty normal, I guess. I haven't noticed any periods like what you're describing.
Over these past two years, have you felt like these messages were being sent to you almost every day?

No, not for the whole two years. It's really just been... well, these beliefs about the school portal and the practicum emails marking me, it's been happening like this for about the past two months. That's when I really knew for sure what they were doing.
When you are speaking with your mom or others, do you find that your sentences sometimes don't make sense or that you have trouble keeping track of what you are trying to say?
No, I don't think so. I mean, my mom and I argue about the emails, but she understands what I'm saying. I don't get confused or lose track of my sentences. I just say what I need to say.

Looking back over the entire two-year period, were there times before these last two months where you felt like you were lacking the motivation or the ability to express yourself, even though you didn't have these specific thoughts about the emails yet?

Well, yeah... even before the last two months, I've just been really... empty, I guess. Mostly I just can't make myself do anything anymore. I just sit in my room, usually in the same clothes for a few days. I don't knit or journal or go for walks like I used to. It's just too much effort. And when my mom comes in and asks what's wrong, I just... I barely have the energy to even answer her. It's just been like that for a long time.

target_item.manifestation: Since I was in those college classes, I've known the school portal and the clinic practicum people were using little wording changes in emails and assignment comments to mark me as someone they don't want in healthcare, even when my mom says they're just regular messages.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about unusual beliefs or experiences, such as feeling a special connection to events or sensing things others cannot. This directly relates to the symptom of delusions, where I have fixed beliefs about the school portal and clinic practicum people sending me hidden messages.

patient.answer: Well, I do have this one thing. Since I was taking those college classes, I've just known that the school portal and the people running the clinic practicum were sending me messages. Like, they were using these little wording changes in emails and assignment comments to mark me as someone they don't want in healthcare. My mom says they're just regular messages, but I know what they're actually saying.

inference.note: The patient's report of a systematized, delusional interpretation of neutral stimuli (the school portal/emails) over the last two years, combined with social withdrawal, avolition, and a lack of overt disorganized thought, shifts the differential toward Schizophreniform disorder or Schizotypal personality disorder. F60.1 is less likely given the clear emergence of delusional ideation.

doctor.intent: Distinguish between Schizotypal Personality Disorder (F21) and Schizophrenia (F20.81) by assessing if the patient's belief is a fixed, systematized delusion.
doctor.question: Do you feel that these messages you are receiving are part of a larger, organized plan or conspiracy that is specifically targeting you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: Since I was in those college classes, I've known the school portal and the clinic practicum people were using little wording changes in emails and assignment comments to mark me as someone they don't want in healthcare, even when my mom says they're just regular messages.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking further about the patient's beliefs regarding the messages from the school portal and practicum people, which falls under the 'Delusions' symptom profile.

patient.answer: Yeah, I mean... like I was just saying, it's definitely a plan to target me. The people running the clinic practicum and whoever runs the school portal, they're doing it together. They're purposely using those little wording changes in my emails and the assignment comments to mark me, so I can't be in healthcare. My mom keeps telling me there's no plan and that they're just normal messages, but... I know they're organized and working together to keep me out.

inference.note: The patient's description of organized, systematized persecutory delusions regarding the school and clinic staff, persisting for over two years, shifts the diagnostic focus toward schizophrenia spectrum disorders. F21 (Schizotypal disorder) is less likely given the fixed, systematized nature of the delusions.

doctor.intent: To determine if the patient has experienced any significant mood symptoms (like depression or mania) during the two-year period, which is crucial for distinguishing between Schizophrenia (F20.0) and Schizophreniform disorder or other related conditions.
doctor.question: During these past two years, have there been any periods where you felt unusually high, irritable, or had so much energy that you didn't need to sleep?

patient.answer: No, I haven't had anything like that happen. I don't really get those high feelings, and I definitely don't have so much energy that I stop sleeping. I just... my energy is pretty normal, I guess. I haven't noticed any periods like what you're describing.

doctor.intent: Determine if there are other symptoms of schizophrenia (such as disorganized speech or behavior) present, or if the clinical picture is dominated by the delusion and the negative symptoms (avolition/social withdrawal).
doctor.question: When you are speaking with your mom or others, do you find that your sentences sometimes don't make sense or that you have trouble keeping track of what you are trying to say?

patient.answer: No, I don't think so. I mean, my mom and I argue about the emails, but she understands what I'm saying. I don't get confused or lose track of my sentences. I just say what I need to say.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced any other symptoms of schizophrenia (such as avolition, alogia, or flattened affect) that have persisted for at least six months, which is required to differentiate schizophrenia (F20.0) from brief psychotic disorder or other conditions.
doctor.question: Looking back over the entire two-year period, were there times before these last two months where you felt like you were lacking the motivation or the ability to express yourself, even though you didn't have these specific thoughts about the emails yet?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: Mostly I just can't make myself do anything anymore—I sit in my room with the same clothes on, don't knit or journal or go walking like I used to, and when my mom asks what's wrong I barely have the energy to answer.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about lacking motivation or the ability to express myself, which directly maps to Negative Symptoms.

patient.answer: Well, yeah... even before the last two months, I've just been really... empty, I guess. Mostly I just can't make myself do anything anymore. I just sit in my room, usually in the same clothes for a few days. I don't knit or journal or go for walks like I used to. It's just too much effort. And when my mom comes in and asks what's wrong, I just... I barely have the energy to even answer her. It's just been like that for a long time.

inference.note: The duration of the negative symptoms (avolition, social withdrawal) exceeds 6 months, and the delusional symptoms have been present for 2 months. This clinical presentation of long-standing negative symptoms with recent onset of delusions points toward Schizophreniform disorder or Schizotypal disorder, though F20.81 remains a strong candidate given the functional decline.
